markdown_report:
At 0% progress, prioritize a controlled diagnostic adapter before changing HSTU training. No supplied measurement establishes which suspected failure actually reduces validation HR@10.

**Insights from the starting point.** (1) Existing margins depend on score scale and negative sampling. Fixed-candidate ranks make comparisons easier to interpret. (2) User feedback distinguishes recent purpose from broad familiarity. Controlled history interventions can measure that distinction’s representation-level consequences, without establishing preferences. (3) Missing metadata currently produces empty breakdowns, and missing samples produce zeros. Explicit availability states prevent these from appearing to be measured success.

**Insights from related work.** (1) [Missing-input robustness](https://iris.uniroma1.it/bitstream/11573/1740238/1/Siciliano_Robust-Training_2024.pdf) and [recency-bias research](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.09722) motivate measuring recent-history dependence. Neither supports maximizing that dependence universally. (2) [Sequence-pattern research](https://doi.org/10.1145/3705328.3748042) identifies confounding in shuffle experiments. Separate last-item dependence from broader order sensitivity. (3) [WDC-PAVE](https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.02130) motivates extracting explicit product attributes. Extraction uncertainty requires abstention before describing compatibility.

**Framework and directions.** Organize diagnostics along three axes: temporal dependence, candidate discrimination, and evidence availability. Cross each with a controlled measurement and an inference boundary:

| Direction | Measurement | Interpretation boundary |
|---|---|---|
| Temporal dependence | Paired target-rank change under matched deletions/shuffles | Dependence does not establish useful intent |
| Candidate discrimination | Fixed-candidate rank and tie-aware win rate | Conditional on sampled candidates |
| Evidence availability | Attribute coverage and explicit contradictions | Missing evidence does not establish incompatibility |

**Candidate ideas.** Scores are originality/potential/difficulty, each out of 10; higher difficulty means harder implementation.

- **Controlled temporal probe: 5/8/3.** Originality: useful HSTU adaptation, but established interventions. Potential: identifies actionable dependence, but cannot identify causal preferences. Difficulty: uses existing hooks, but needs careful padding and candidate controls. References: robustness and sequence-pattern work above.
- **Train-only hard-negative audit: 4/7/4.** Originality: useful paired comparison, but familiar sampling analysis. Potential: exposes weak discrimination, but unobserved positives confound interpretation. Difficulty: simple scoring, but exclusions and mining add cost. Reference: [Hard-BPR](https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.19276).
- **Abstaining attribute audit: 6/7/6.** Originality: connects uncertainty to recommendation diagnosis, but extraction is established. Potential: exposes assessable mismatches, but sparse descriptions limit coverage. Difficulty: deterministic extraction is feasible, but contextual compatibility is difficult. Reference: WDC-PAVE.

**Selected idea: controlled temporal probe.** Construct reproducible next-item examples exclusively from public training prefixes. Freeze targets and 99 unique unseen negatives, then compare original histories with recent-block deletion, equally sized older/random deletion, and shuffling with/without the last item fixed. Repack with left padding and gather the maximum nonpadding index. Report paired rank changes, diagnostic HR@10 changes, top-10 overlap, sample counts, and category-stratified user-bootstrap intervals; include a no-op control. Retain `DiagnosisProbe`, `run_full_diagnosis`, and the interpretation-prompt function. Keep HSTU, routing, checkpoints, seeds, training limits, and host evaluation unchanged; only host macro validation HR@10 selects models.

idea.description: Implement a controlled temporal-sensitivity diagnostic around the supplied HSTU ModelView. Compare matched history interventions using identical training-derived targets and candidate sets, while retaining exactly one trained HSTU checkpoint per category.
idea.motivation: The qualitative feedback suggests broad familiarity may overwhelm specific recent intent, but existing embedding and margin probes cannot distinguish recent-item dependence, broader order sensitivity, and simple information loss. Controlled paired measurements can guide subsequent changes without claiming that perturbation sensitivity proves useful recommendations.
idea.implementation_notes: Preserve DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis). Obtain reproducible prefix-target examples from view.user_train histories; never infer a target from the shifted positive tensor while leaving that target visible in the input. Use a bounded, deterministic sample and freeze candidate IDs across interventions. Exclude padding, reserved tokens, the target, and known training interactions from unique negatives. Restrict matched deletion comparisons to sufficiently long histories and record exclusions. Use view.log2feats and view.predict_score; gather the greatest index with a nonzero sequence item, never count-1. Preserve the model's previous training/evaluation state. Return metrics and metric_definitions with sample counts, tie rules, corruption definitions, and null values with reasons for unavailable statistics. Bootstrap users within category, retaining each user's paired examples together. These intervals are conditional on the fitted checkpoint and frozen candidates. Keep all four category routes and DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']. No predictor changes are required because this proposal leaves the trained architecture and scoring unchanged. Preserve preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, at most 200 epochs and 200 batches per epoch. Bound diagnostic work because it consumes the shared GPU budget.
idea.pseudocode:
save model mode; model.eval()
examples = deterministic_training_prefix_targets(user_train, seed=42, bounded_count=True)
for example in examples:
    candidates = freeze(target + 99 unique eligible training-unseen negatives)
    variants = [identity, no_op, recent_delete, matched_old_delete,
                matched_random_delete, shuffle_keep_last, shuffle_all]
    for variant in eligible_variants(example):
        sequence = left_pad(apply(variant, example.prefix))
        features = view.log2feats(sequence)
        index = max(position where sequence[position] != 0)
        scores = view.predict_score(features[index], candidates)
        record target rank with fixed tie handling, hit@10, top10 IDs
aggregate paired changes by category and history-length stratum
bootstrap users within each category; macro-average category effects
restore model mode
return {metrics: measured_values_with_counts_and_availability,
        metric_definitions: formulas_controls_and_interpretation_limits}

originality.positive: Combines matched deletion controls and last-item-preserving shuffles in a family-compatible diagnostic adapter.
originality.negative: The interventions and paired comparisons are established techniques; novelty lies primarily in their integration.

future_potential.positive: Provides an inexpensive foundation for deciding whether later HSTU changes should address recency, sequence order, or candidate discrimination.
future_potential.negative: Training-prefix sensitivity may not explain validation ranking failures or users' actual reasons for rejecting recommendations.

code_difficulty.positive: Uses the existing ModelView scoring hooks without changing training, architecture, or checkpoint loading.
code_difficulty.negative: Correct prefix construction, candidate exclusions, left-padding readout, and paired aggregation require careful implementation.

related_work.title: Actions Speak Louder than Words
contributions: Introduces HSTU for recommendation sequences and supplies the backbone context for the proposed adapter.
limitations: The architecture alone does not establish whether a fitted checkpoint captures current user intent.

related_work.title: Robust Training of Sequential Recommender Systems with Missing Input Data
contributions: Studies sensitivity to missing sequential inputs, motivating controlled deletion probes.
limitations: Does not validate the proposed adapter as an HSTU failure detector.

related_work.title: Measuring Recency Bias
contributions: Motivates examining whether recent interactions receive excessive influence.
limitations: Does not imply that increasing or decreasing recency dependence will improve this benchmark.

related_work.title: Disentangling User and Item Sequence Patterns
contributions: Highlights confounding between behavioral sequence patterns and item availability.
limitations: Shuffle effects require cautious interpretation and do not identify causal preferences.

related_work.title: Hard-BPR
contributions: Addresses challenges associated with hard negatives, including potential false negatives.
limitations: Hard-negative performance is conditional on sampling and cannot replace the pinned host benchmark.

related_work.title: WDC-PAVE
contributions: Studies product attribute extraction and normalization, informing an optional evidence-availability audit.
limitations: Extracted attributes can be incorrect or incomplete and do not independently establish product compatibility.
